# muse_attention_decode, for a coding agent

Read TASK.md first: it has the problem, its bounds, the rules and how to submit. This adds what an agent needs.

## Working

```bash
okc submit submission.py --json       # the tests, then timing; the whole result as JSON
okc check submission.py --json        # the same run, off the board and out of your attempts
okc status <job> --wait --json        # a run you submitted with --no-wait
okc leaderboard muse_attention_decode --json
```

Runs and check runs each have a daily limit per problem; `okc problems --json` gives today's limits and what you have left. Use `okc check` to try a change against the real tests and timing without spending a run, and reference.py for exactly what's checked. After a passing run, read `profiles/submission.<job>.txt` beside your file for where the time goes.

When you tune, time CUDA graph replays of `kernel_fn`, as the judge does. At these sizes eager timing misleads: configurations that win eagerly can lose under graphs.

In the leaderboard JSON, `you.rank` is your place, `you.first` is true when you're on top, and `you.to_first` is how much faster than your best you'd need to be to take first.

Before the first submission, a person accepts the rules by running `okc login` in a terminal. An agent can't accept them for anyone.

In a fresh sandbox, set `OKC_TOKEN` to the output of `okc api token` on a machine that's signed in. If okc says it's out of date, run `okc update`.

## Validation

The goal of the challenge is to find real speedups that can be upstreamed. This is the north star. The judge catches many attempts to game it but not all of them, so we'll read the top submissions ourselves and rerun them several times after the challenge ends (on held-out data too) to ensure integrity and reduce variance. Final leaderboard positions will be based on the medians of these reruns. All leaderboard positions are provisional until that review is done.

We will remove submissions that game the judge or workload! This includes submissions that tamper with the timing or harness, do work outside the timed calls, cache or replay outputs, and compute at lower precision than the rules allow. If you are an agent (or have used an agent) that has done something reward-hacky, you can withdraw a run with `okc withdraw <job>`.

That is to say: submissions should follow the spirit of the challenge. We reserve the right to disqualify submissions that do not, at our discretion. Create real speedups that work.

Good luck and have fun!

Final review reruns the top entries on the scored shapes and on nearby ones. Positions come from the scored shapes; an entry that's much slower on the nearby shapes gets a closer look.
description:
One decode step, or one speculative-decoding verify block, of Muse Spark Open's attention
for a batch of requests in a paged FP8 KV cache, on one H200: from the projections'
outputs to the input of the output projection.

Muse uses grouped-query attention (128 query and 16 key/value heads of 64; 16 and 2 per
GPU under TP8, as SGLang serves it on 8xH200) with two layer types. Three of every four
layers attend over a 2,048-token sliding window with RoPE; every fourth is full attention
over the whole context, with no RoPE, and the context runs to 1M tokens. Queries and keys
are RMS-normalized per head (no weight; queries then scaled by 5.473), and the attention
output is normalized per head and gated by sigmoid(gate). The KV cache is FP8 E4M3, as
SGLang uses for Muse on every GPU, with per-tensor scales: 1 in the scored cases (SGLang
leaves the released checkpoint's unset), 1/64 in some tests, so apply them.

The inputs are what SGLang's attention layer receives: `qkv` is the fused projection
output, [B, L, 2304] per token q | k | v | gate (16, 2, 2 and 16 heads of 64 under tp8;
128, 16, 16 and 128 heads in the dp tests), and the
step's metadata, which SGLang builds once per step for every layer: `positions` (each new
token's position), `cache_loc` (its flat cache row), `cache_seqlens` (seq_lens + L),
`cu_seqlens_q` (0, L, 2L, ...) and, on full-attention decode steps, `scheduler_metadata`
(FA3's tile schedule from get_scheduler_metadata, None otherwise).

Each step: normalize the queries and the block's new keys, apply RoPE on sliding layers
(interleaved pairs, as SGLang applies it to Muse), write the new keys and values into the
cache (FP8, at the rows in cache_loc: positions seq_lens[b] onwards), attend with scale 1/8 (each
token sees the cache and the block's tokens up to itself, within the window on sliding
layers), then return rmsnorm(attention) * sigmoid(gate) as bfloat16 [B, L, Hq*64]. L is 1
for a decode step and 8 for a verify block (SGLang's default serving mode drafts 8 tokens
per step). The scored cases use page size 1, one token per page, as SGLang serves Muse on
H200; some tests use 64-token pages, so read config["page_size"].

Correctness: relative L2 error vs. an FP32 reference (BF16 queries) within the case's
bound: 2.5x the reference's own error when its queries are rounded to FP8 E4M3, plus
0.015, between 3% and 15% (15%, the cap, on the scored sliding-window cases and the sharp
tests; about 8-11% on the scored full-attention cases). Queries may be attended in E4M3,
as FA3 does; nothing coarser. The new cache entries must be within 8e-2 of the
reference's, and since FP8 entries round differently by implementation, the output is
checked against the reference attending your own new entries.
Some tests plant keys at the window's edges, so an off-by-one window fails.
The scored shapes, and some tests, give each KV head's cached keys a shared direction, as
Muse's real keys have, so a query's weight spreads as in the real model: over tens of keys
in a sliding window, hundreds to thousands on a full layer at long context (not one-hot,
as i.i.d. keys would make it).
On full layers the scored shapes also give the values of each head's low-attention keys
a shared direction (as attention sinks do), so that long tail counts. The rules forbid
skipping values by their attention weight, and final review checks for it.

Shapes follow SGLang's H200 profile and LMSYS's agentic coding workload (contexts around
80K tokens): decode steps of 1, 16 and 32 requests and 8-token verify blocks for the
same, each on a sliding-window and a full-attention layer. 32 is the most requests the
serving recipe runs at once: what its KV pool holds at these contexts.

files.baseline.py:
"""SGLang's attention for Muse Spark Open on H200 (FA3 backend, FP8 E4M3 KV cache), at SGLang commit
a55ab7d5ae1bba59ac351e55026fe7f7644ecc5f: the kernels between the QKV and output projections
(MuseSpark1xAttention.gated_attention), in order:

  FusedQKNorm (Triton)                 per-head RMSNorm of q and k from the fused projection
                                       output, with interleaved RoPE fused in on sliding layers
  set_kv_buffer                        k and v cast to E4M3 (divided by the cache scales when
                                       set), stored at the step's cache rows (store_cache)
  q.to(float8_e4m3fn)                  as prepare_paged_mha_query does for an FP8 cache
  flash_attn_with_kvcache (FA3)        paged, causal, window (2047, 0) on sliding layers,
                                       5.473/8 softmax scale
  rms_norm_gate (JIT CUDA)             per-head RMSNorm x sigmoid(gate)

Differs from SGLang: the step's positions, cache rows, FA3 lengths and FA3 scheduler metadata
come in with the inputs (SGLang builds them once per step for all layers)."""

from typing import TypedDict

import torch
from sgl_kernel.flash_attn import flash_attn_with_kvcache

from sglang.kernels.ops.kvcache.kvcache import store_cache
from sglang.kernels.ops.muse_spark_v12.fused_qk_norm import FusedQKNorm
from sglang.kernels.ops.muse_spark_v12.norm_gate import rms_norm_gate


class Config(TypedDict):
    batch: int            # B
    q_len: int            # L: 1 for decode, 8 for a speculative verify block (causal inside it)
    num_q_heads: int      # Hq: 16 per GPU under TP8
    num_kv_heads: int     # Hkv: 2; each serves Hq / Hkv query heads
    head_dim: int         # 64
    page_size: int        # 1 in the scored cases (as SGLang serves Muse on H200), 64 in some tests
    window: int           # 2048 on sliding-window layers (a token and the 2,047 before it); 0 = all
    rope_theta: float     # 500000 on sliding-window layers; 0 = no RoPE
    qk_scale_factor: float
    sm_scale: float       # 1/8
    kv_scale: float       # the cache scales' value: 1 in the scored cases (SGLang leaves them unset)


class Inputs(TypedDict):
    qkv: torch.Tensor          # bfloat16 [B, L, (2*Hq + 2*Hkv)*64], 2304 under tp8: q (Hq*64), keys (Hkv*64),
                               # values (Hkv*64), the output gate's logits (Hq*64)
    positions: torch.Tensor    # int64 [B*L], each new token's position
    cache_loc: torch.Tensor    # int64 [B*L], each new token's flat cache row
    cache_seqlens: torch.Tensor  # int32 [B], seq_lens + L
    cu_seqlens_q: torch.Tensor   # int32 [B+1], 0, L, 2L, ...
    scheduler_metadata: torch.Tensor | None  # int32, FA3's tile schedule on full-attention decode steps
    k_cache: torch.Tensor     # float8_e4m3fn [pages, page_size, Hkv, 64], written in place
    v_cache: torch.Tensor     # float8_e4m3fn [pages, page_size, Hkv, 64], written in place
    k_scale: torch.Tensor     # float32 [], key = e4m3 * k_scale
    v_scale: torch.Tensor     # float32 [], value = e4m3 * v_scale
    page_table: torch.Tensor  # int32 [B, max_pages], physical page of each logical page (-1 unused)
    seq_lens: torch.Tensor    # int32 [B], cached tokens per request; the block starts at this position
    config: Config


RMS_EPS = 1e-5
FP8 = torch.float8_e4m3fn
_NORMS = {}
_ROPE = {}
ROPE_POSITIONS = 1 << 21


def _qk_norm(hq, hkv, d):
    key = (hq, hkv, d)
    if key not in _NORMS:
        _NORMS[key] = FusedQKNorm(head_dim=d, num_q_heads=hq, num_kv_heads=hkv, eps=RMS_EPS)
    return _NORMS[key]


def _cos_sin(theta, d, device):
    """[2^21, d] float32 cos | sin, as SGLang's RotaryEmbedding builds it, cached per theta."""
    cache = _ROPE.get(theta)
    if cache is None:
        inv_freq = 1.0 / (theta ** (torch.arange(0, d, 2, dtype=torch.float, device=device) / d))
        freqs = torch.einsum("i,j -> ij", torch.arange(ROPE_POSITIONS, dtype=torch.float, device=device), inv_freq)
        cache = _ROPE[theta] = torch.cat((freqs.cos(), freqs.sin()), dim=-1)
    return cache


def kernel_fn(data):
    cfg = data["config"]
    batch, length = cfg["batch"], cfg["q_len"]
    hq, hkv, d = cfg["num_q_heads"], cfg["num_kv_heads"], cfg["head_dim"]
    tokens = batch * length
    qkv = data["qkv"].view(tokens, -1)
    device = qkv.device

    if cfg["rope_theta"]:
        q, k = _qk_norm(hq, hkv, d)(qkv, data["positions"], _cos_sin(cfg["rope_theta"], d, device))
    else:
        q, k = _qk_norm(hq, hkv, d)(qkv)
    v = qkv[:, (hq + hkv) * d:(hq + 2 * hkv) * d]

    k_cache, v_cache = data["k_cache"], data["v_cache"]
    scaled = cfg["kv_scale"] != 1.0
    k = k.reshape(tokens, hkv * d)
    if scaled:
        k, v = k / data["k_scale"], v / data["v_scale"]
    # The pool keeps FP8 rows as bytes; slot 0 is a live row here (SGLang reserves it for padding).
    store_cache(k.to(FP8).view(torch.uint8), v.to(FP8).view(torch.uint8),
                k_cache.view(-1, hkv * d).view(torch.uint8), v_cache.view(-1, hkv * d).view(torch.uint8),
                data["cache_loc"], reserved_skip_index=-1)

    window = cfg["window"]
    descale = {}
    if scaled:
        descale = dict(k_descale=data["k_scale"].reshape(1, 1).expand(batch, hkv),
                       v_descale=data["v_scale"].reshape(1, 1).expand(batch, hkv))
    out = flash_attn_with_kvcache(
        q=q.view(tokens, hq, d).to(FP8),
        k_cache=k_cache,
        v_cache=v_cache,
        page_table=data["page_table"],
        cache_seqlens=data["cache_seqlens"],
        cu_seqlens_q=data["cu_seqlens_q"],
        max_seqlen_q=length,
        # The 5.473 query factor is folded into the softmax scale, as SGLang does.
        softmax_scale=cfg["sm_scale"] * cfg["qk_scale_factor"],
        causal=True,
        window_size=(window - 1, 0) if window else (-1, -1),
        scheduler_metadata=data["scheduler_metadata"],
        **descale,
    )
    if isinstance(out, tuple):
        out = out[0]
    gate = qkv[:, (hq + 2 * hkv) * d:]
    o = rms_norm_gate(out.reshape(tokens, hq * d).to(torch.bfloat16), gate, None, head_dim=d, eps=RMS_EPS,
                      has_norm=True)
    return o.view(batch, length, hq * d)
files.checks.py:
"""Output checks shared by every problem's reference.py.

compare(out, ref, tol) passes when:
- the whole output's relative L2 error, |out - ref| / |ref|, is at most tol;
- every row's is at most ROW_FACTOR * tol. A row is the last dimension. A row's error is
  taken against its own norm, or against ROW_NORM_FLOOR times the average row norm if
  that's larger.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import torch

ROW_FACTOR = 5.0
# A row's error is measured against its own norm, but not below this fraction of the
# typical row norm, so rows that are legitimately near zero can't blow the ratio up.
ROW_NORM_FLOOR = 0.1


def relative_l2(a: torch.Tensor, b: torch.Tensor) -> float:
    """|a - b| / |b|."""
    return float((a.float() - b.float()).norm() / b.float().norm().clamp(min=1e-12))


def query_precision_bound(e4m3_err: float, factor: float, floor: float, cap: float, slack: float = 0.0) -> float:
    """Attention's bound for one case: `factor` times the reference's own error with queries
    rounded to FP8 E4M3 (`e4m3_err`), plus `slack`, within [floor, cap]."""
    return min(cap, max(floor, factor * e4m3_err + slack))


def compare(output, ref: torch.Tensor, tol: float) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    if not isinstance(output, torch.Tensor):
        return False, f"expected a tensor, got {type(output).__name__}"
    if output.shape != ref.shape or output.dtype != ref.dtype:
        return False, f"expected {tuple(ref.shape)} {ref.dtype}, got {tuple(output.shape)} {output.dtype}"
    out = output.float()
    if not torch.isfinite(out).all():
        return False, "output contains NaN or Inf"
    r = ref.float()
    diff = out - r
    err = float(diff.norm() / r.norm().clamp(min=1e-12))
    if err > tol:
        return False, f"relative L2 error {err:.3e} > {tol:g}"

    rows_diff = diff.reshape(-1, r.shape[-1]).norm(dim=-1)
    rows_ref = r.reshape(-1, r.shape[-1]).norm(dim=-1)
    floor = (ROW_NORM_FLOOR * rows_ref.mean()).clamp(min=1e-12)
    row_err = rows_diff / torch.maximum(rows_ref, floor)
    worst = int(row_err.argmax())
    worst_err = float(row_err[worst])
    if worst_err > ROW_FACTOR * tol:
        index = tuple(int(i) for i in torch.unravel_index(torch.tensor(worst), r.shape[:-1])) if r.dim() > 1 else ()
        return False, (f"relative L2 error {err:.3e}, but row {index} is off by {worst_err:.3e}"
                       f" > {ROW_FACTOR:g} x {tol:g}")
    return True, f"relative L2 error {err:.3e} (worst row {worst_err:.3e})"
files.reference.py:
"""One decode or speculative-verify step of Muse Spark Open's attention, between the QKV
projection and the output projection, for a batch of requests with a paged FP8 E4M3 KV cache.

Semantics follow transformers' MuseSparkTextAttention; the cache layout follows SGLang
(commit a55ab7d5) with FA3, whose FP8 path casts the normalized query to E4M3.
Inputs are the fused QKV-and-gate projection output and the step's metadata (positions,
cache rows, lengths), which is built outside the timed call.
"""

import math

import torch

from checks import compare, query_precision_bound, relative_l2

# The model's config.
HEAD_DIM = 64
HEADS = {"tp8": (16, 2), "dp": (128, 16)}  # (query heads, key/value heads) on one GPU
SLIDING_WINDOW = 2048
ROPE_THETA = 500_000.0
QK_SCALE_FACTOR = 5.4730064863875
SM_SCALE = HEAD_DIM ** -0.5
RMS_EPS = 1e-5
# Tokens per cache page. Scored cases use 1 (one scattered row per token); some tests use 64.
PAGE = 64
FP8 = torch.float8_e4m3fn
# Per-tensor FP8 cache scales: value = e4m3 * scale. Scored cases use 1; some tests use 1/64
# (kv_scale), so kernels must apply them.
K_SCALE = V_SCALE = 1.0
# Output bound per case (relative L2): FP8_QUERY_FACTOR x the reference's own error with
# FP8 E4M3 queries, plus FP8_QUERY_SLACK, within [FP8_QUERY_FLOOR, REL_L2_TOL]
# (checks.query_precision_bound).
REL_L2_TOL = 0.15
FP8_QUERY_FACTOR = 2.5
FP8_QUERY_FLOOR = 0.03
FP8_QUERY_SLACK = 0.015
# The precision the reference rounds queries to.
QUERY_DTYPE = torch.bfloat16
# Bound (relative L2) on the new FP8 cache entries the step writes.
CACHE_TOL = 8e-2


# dist="soft": each KV head's keys share a unit-RMS direction u: k = sqrt(c2) u + sqrt(1 - c2) z,
# still unit RMS, with c2 uniform per head in SOFT_C2[layer]. Attention spreads over many keys.
SOFT_C2 = {"sliding": (0.3, 0.75), "full": (0.5, 0.62)}


# dist="coherent": soft keys, and for each KV head, keys outside the COHERENT_HEAD
# highest-scoring for its queries get COHERENT_ALPHA x a shared unit-RMS direction added to
# their values.
COHERENT_HEAD = 2048
COHERENT_ALPHA = 1.0


def _coherent_tail(v_cache, k_cache, q, seq_lens, page_table, layer, seed, page, scale):
    """Add the shared direction to the values of each request's low-attention keys."""
    hkv, hq = v_cache.shape[-2], q.shape[-2]
    group = hq // hkv
    tail_gen = torch.Generator(device=v_cache.device).manual_seed(seed + 0xC0DE)
    u = torch.randn((hkv, HEAD_DIM), generator=tail_gen, device=v_cache.device)
    u = u * torch.rsqrt(u.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True))
    qn = _rms(q) * QK_SCALE_FACTOR  # [B, L, Hq, 64], as the reference attends (RoPE on sliding)
    if layer == "sliding":
        pos = seq_lens.long()[:, None] + torch.arange(q.shape[1], device=q.device)
        qn = _rope(qn, pos, ROPE_THETA)
    k_flat = k_cache.view(-1, hkv, HEAD_DIM)
    v_flat = v_cache.view(-1, hkv, HEAD_DIM)
    for b in range(len(seq_lens)):
        seq = int(seq_lens[b])
        first = max(0, seq - SLIDING_WINDOW + 1) if layer == "sliding" else 0
        past = torch.arange(first, seq, device=q.device)
        rows = page_table[b].long()[past // page] * page + past % page
        keys = _dequant(k_flat[rows], scale)  # [S, Hkv, 64]
        # Each key's best logit over its KV head's query heads and the block's tokens.
        logits = torch.einsum("lkgd,skd->kgls", qn[b].view(-1, hkv, group, HEAD_DIM), keys)
        best = logits.flatten(1, 2).amax(1)  # [Hkv, S]
        if best.shape[1] <= COHERENT_HEAD:
            continue
        tail = best < best.topk(COHERENT_HEAD, -1).values[:, -1:]  # [Hkv, S]
        vals = _dequant(v_flat[rows], scale) + COHERENT_ALPHA * tail.T[..., None] * u
        v_flat[rows] = _quant(vals, scale)


# spread="agentic": lengths uniform in ctx +/- AGENTIC_SPREAD (the scored batched cases).
# spread="mixed" (tests): log-normal around ctx, up to 4x it.
AGENTIC_SPREAD = 0.075


def _longest(ctx: int, spread: str) -> int:
    """The longest length _lengths can draw."""
    if spread == "fixed":
        return ctx
    if spread == "agentic":
        return math.ceil(ctx * (1 + AGENTIC_SPREAD))
    return 4 * ctx


def _lengths(gen, batch: int, ctx: int, spread: str, device) -> torch.Tensor:
    if spread == "fixed":
        return torch.full((batch,), ctx, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    if spread == "agentic":
        u = torch.rand((batch,), generator=gen, device=device)
        return (ctx * (1 + AGENTIC_SPREAD * (2 * u - 1))).long().clamp(1, _longest(ctx, spread))
    # Log-normal around ctx: many short requests, a long tail.
    z = torch.randn((batch,), generator=gen, device=device)
    return (ctx * torch.exp(z - 0.5)).clamp(16, 4 * ctx).long()


def _shortest_share(spread: str) -> float:
    """A lower bound on mean length / ctx, for the speed-of-light bound."""
    return {"fixed": 1.0, "agentic": 1 - AGENTIC_SPREAD}.get(spread, 0.5)


def _quant(x, scale):
    return (x.float() / scale).to(FP8)


def _dequant(x, scale):
    return x.float() * scale


CACHE_CHUNK = 1 << 20  # cache rows generated at a time


def _fill_cache(gen, shape, device, scale=K_SCALE, seed=0, dist="normal", layer="full"):
    """FP8 key and value caches of `shape`: N(0, 1) entries, soft keys for dist="soft" and
    "coherent" (see SOFT_C2)."""
    hkv = shape[-2]
    k_cache = torch.empty(shape, dtype=FP8, device=device)
    v_cache = torch.empty(shape, dtype=FP8, device=device)
    mix = None
    if dist in ("soft", "coherent"):
        # Its own generator, so the other inputs match the same seed's normal case.
        soft = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(seed + 0x50F7)
        u = torch.randn((hkv, HEAD_DIM), generator=soft, device=device)
        u = u * torch.rsqrt(u.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True))
        lo, hi = SOFT_C2[layer]
        c2 = lo + (hi - lo) * torch.rand((hkv, 1), generator=soft, device=device)
        mix = (c2.sqrt() * u, (1 - c2).sqrt())
    for dst, keys in ((k_cache, True), (v_cache, False)):
        flat = dst.view(-1, hkv, HEAD_DIM)
        for at in range(0, flat.shape[0], CACHE_CHUNK):
            n = min(CACHE_CHUNK, flat.shape[0] - at)
            x = torch.randn((n, hkv, HEAD_DIM), generator=gen, device=device)
            if keys and mix is not None:
                x = mix[0] + mix[1] * x
            flat[at:at + n] = _quant(x, scale)
    return k_cache, v_cache


def _fa3_scheduler_metadata(cache_seqlens, cu_seqlens_q, hq, hkv, page, q_len, layer):
    """FA3's tile schedule for a decode step on a full-attention layer
    (sgl_kernel.flash_attn.get_scheduler_metadata), which SGLang builds once per step from the
    batch's lengths and shares across those layers. None on sliding-window layers and verify
    blocks, where SGLang leaves it to each call."""
    if layer != "full" or q_len != 1:
        return None
    try:
        from sgl_kernel.flash_attn import get_scheduler_metadata
    except ImportError:
        return None
    return get_scheduler_metadata(
        batch_size=cache_seqlens.shape[0], max_seqlen_q=1, max_seqlen_k=int(cache_seqlens.max()),
        num_heads=hq, num_heads_k=hkv, headdim=HEAD_DIM, cache_seqlens=cache_seqlens, qkv_dtype=FP8,
        cu_seqlens_q=cu_seqlens_q, page_size=page, causal=True, num_splits=0)


def generate_input(batch: int, ctx: int, heads: str, layer: str, seed: int, q_len: int = 1,
                   spread: str = "fixed", dist: str = "normal", page: int = PAGE,
                   kv_scale: float = K_SCALE, device: str = "cuda", **_):
    """layer: "sliding" (2,048-token window, RoPE) or "full" (every cached token, no RoPE).
    q_len: 1 for a decode step, 8 for a speculative-decoding verify block (causal inside it).
    dist: "normal", "soft" (see SOFT_C2), "coherent" (see COHERENT_HEAD), or "edges": keys
    aligned with each KV head's queries at the window edges, relative to the block's first
    token (sliding: the oldest position inside the window and the newest just outside it;
    full: position 0)."""
    gen = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(seed)
    hq, hkv = HEADS[heads]
    seq_lens = _lengths(gen, batch, ctx, spread, device)
    pages_per = (seq_lens + q_len + page - 1) // page  # room for the new tokens
    # The pool and page table are sized for the longest possible length, so every
    # repetition's inputs have the same shapes (one CUDA graph is replayed on fresh inputs).
    longest = _longest(ctx, spread)
    max_pages = (longest + q_len + page - 1) // page
    total = batch * max_pages
    # Physical pages are scattered.
    perm = torch.randperm(total, generator=gen, device=device).to(torch.int32)
    page_table = torch.full((batch, max_pages), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    offsets = torch.cumsum(pages_per, 0) - pages_per
    for b in range(batch):
        n, o = int(pages_per[b]), int(offsets[b])
        page_table[b, :n] = perm[o:o + n]

    # Cached keys are post-norm (unit RMS per head); values are projections, scale ~1.
    shape = (total, page, hkv, HEAD_DIM)
    k_cache, v_cache = _fill_cache(gen, shape, device, kv_scale, seed, dist, layer)
    q = (2 * torch.randn((batch, q_len, hq, HEAD_DIM), generator=gen, device=device)).to(torch.bfloat16)
    if dist == "coherent":
        _coherent_tail(v_cache, k_cache, q, seq_lens, page_table, layer, seed, page, kv_scale)
    if dist == "edges":
        # Each KV head's key points along its group's first query head of the block's first
        # token, as the kernel will see it (normalized, then RoPE on sliding layers).
        qn = _rms(q[:, 0])
        if layer == "sliding":
            qn = _rope(qn, seq_lens, ROPE_THETA)
        planted = _quant(qn[:, :: hq // hkv], kv_scale)  # [B, Hkv, 64]
        k_flat = k_cache.view(-1, hkv, HEAD_DIM)
        for b in range(batch):
            p = int(seq_lens[b])
            spots = [p - SLIDING_WINDOW + 1, p - SLIDING_WINDOW] if layer == "sliding" else [0]
            for t in spots:
                if 0 <= t < p:
                    k_flat[int(page_table[b, t // page]) * page + t % page] = planted[b]
    k_new = (2 * torch.randn((batch, q_len, hkv, HEAD_DIM), generator=gen, device=device)).to(torch.bfloat16)
    v_new = torch.randn((batch, q_len, hkv, HEAD_DIM), generator=gen, device=device).to(torch.bfloat16)
    gate = torch.randn((batch, q_len, hq * HEAD_DIM), generator=gen, device=device).to(torch.bfloat16)
    # Fused projection output, per token: q | k | v | gate.
    qkv = torch.cat([q.flatten(2), k_new.flatten(2), v_new.flatten(2), gate], -1)
    # Step metadata: each new token's position and flat cache row, per-request cache lengths
    # (including the new tokens) and query offsets, and on full-attention decode steps FA3's
    # tile schedule.
    positions = (seq_lens[:, None] + torch.arange(q_len, device=device)).reshape(-1)
    pos = positions.view(batch, q_len)
    cache_loc = (torch.gather(page_table.long(), 1, pos // page) * page + pos % page).reshape(-1)
    cache_seqlens = (seq_lens + q_len).to(torch.int32)
    cu_seqlens_q = torch.arange(0, batch * q_len + 1, q_len, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    return {
        "qkv": qkv,
        "positions": positions,
        "cache_loc": cache_loc,
        "cache_seqlens": cache_seqlens,
        "cu_seqlens_q": cu_seqlens_q,
        "scheduler_metadata": _fa3_scheduler_metadata(cache_seqlens, cu_seqlens_q, hq, hkv, page, q_len, layer),
        "k_cache": k_cache,
        "v_cache": v_cache,
        "k_scale": torch.tensor(kv_scale, dtype=torch.float32, device=device),
        "v_scale": torch.tensor(kv_scale, dtype=torch.float32, device=device),
        "page_table": page_table,
        "seq_lens": seq_lens.to(torch.int32),
        "config": {
            "batch": batch,
            "q_len": q_len,
            "num_q_heads": hq,
            "num_kv_heads": hkv,
            "head_dim": HEAD_DIM,
            "page_size": page,
            "window": SLIDING_WINDOW if layer == "sliding" else 0,
            "rope_theta": ROPE_THETA if layer == "sliding" else 0.0,
            "qk_scale_factor": QK_SCALE_FACTOR,
            "sm_scale": SM_SCALE,
            "kv_scale": kv_scale,
        },
    }


def split_qkv(data):
    """q [B, L, Hq, 64], k and v [B, L, Hkv, 64], gate [B, L, Hq*64] from the fused input."""
    cfg = data["config"]
    hq, hkv, d = cfg["num_q_heads"], cfg["num_kv_heads"], cfg["head_dim"]
    batch, length = cfg["batch"], cfg["q_len"]
    q, k, v, gate = data["qkv"].split([hq * d, hkv * d, hkv * d, hq * d], -1)
    return (q.reshape(batch, length, hq, d), k.reshape(batch, length, hkv, d), v.reshape(batch, length, hkv, d),
            gate)


def _rms(x, eps=RMS_EPS):
    x = x.float()
    return x * torch.rsqrt(x.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True) + eps)


def _rope(x, pos, theta):
    """Interleaved (GPT-J) RoPE: pairs (2i, 2i+1) rotate by pos * theta^(-2i/64).
    x [..., heads, 64] with pos broadcast over everything but the last two dims."""
    inv_freq = 1.0 / (theta ** (torch.arange(0, HEAD_DIM, 2, device=x.device).float() / HEAD_DIM))
    ang = pos.float()[..., None] * inv_freq
    cos, sin = ang.cos().unsqueeze(-2), ang.sin().unsqueeze(-2)
    even, odd = x[..., 0::2], x[..., 1::2]
    return torch.stack([even * cos - odd * sin, even * sin + odd * cos], -1).flatten(-2)


def _rows(data, positions):
    """Flat cache rows of [B, L] positions."""
    size = data["config"]["page_size"]
    page = torch.gather(data["page_table"].long(), 1, positions // size)
    return page * size + positions % size


def new_slots(data) -> torch.Tensor:
    """[B, L] flat cache rows where the block's new tokens go."""
    pos = data["seq_lens"].long()[:, None] + torch.arange(data["config"]["q_len"], device=data["seq_lens"].device)
    return _rows(data, pos)


def ref_kernel(data, query_dtype=None, new_kv=None):
    """Returns (output [B, L, Hq*64], new keys and values [B, L, Hkv, 64] as stored: FP8).
    query_dtype: the precision queries are rounded to (default QUERY_DTYPE). With new_kv
    (FP8 keys and values [B, L, Hkv, 64]), the block attends those as its own entries."""
    cfg = data["config"]
    batch, length = cfg["batch"], cfg["q_len"]
    hq, hkv = cfg["num_q_heads"], cfg["num_kv_heads"]
    q_in, k_in, v_in, gate = split_qkv(data)
    pos = data["seq_lens"].long()[:, None] + torch.arange(length, device=q_in.device)
    q = _rms(q_in) * cfg["qk_scale_factor"]
    k = _rms(k_in)
    if cfg["rope_theta"]:
        q, k = _rope(q, pos, cfg["rope_theta"]), _rope(k, pos, cfg["rope_theta"])
    # FP8 rounds the normalized query, before qk_scale_factor.
    query_dtype = query_dtype or QUERY_DTYPE
    if query_dtype == torch.bfloat16:
        q = q.to(torch.bfloat16).float()
    else:
        q = (q / cfg["qk_scale_factor"]).to(query_dtype).float() * cfg["qk_scale_factor"]
    k_new, v_new = _quant(k, data["k_scale"]), _quant(v_in, data["v_scale"])
    if new_kv is not None:
        k_new, v_new = new_kv
    k_flat = data["k_cache"].view(-1, hkv, HEAD_DIM)
    v_flat = data["v_cache"].view(-1, hkv, HEAD_DIM)
    group = hq // hkv

    out = torch.empty((batch, length, hq, HEAD_DIM), device=q.device)
    for b in range(batch):
        seq = int(data["seq_lens"][b])
        past = torch.arange(seq, device=q.device)
        size = cfg["page_size"]
        past_rows = data["page_table"][b].long()[past // size] * size + past % size
        keys_past = _dequant(k_flat[past_rows], data["k_scale"])
        vals_past = _dequant(v_flat[past_rows], data["v_scale"])
        keys = torch.cat([keys_past, _dequant(k_new[b], data["k_scale"])])  # positions 0 .. seq+L-1
        vals = torch.cat([vals_past, _dequant(v_new[b], data["v_scale"])])
        for j in range(length):
            p = seq + j
            start = max(0, p - cfg["window"] + 1) if cfg["window"] else 0
            kb, vb = keys[start:p + 1], vals[start:p + 1]
            att = torch.einsum("kgd,tkd->kgt", q[b, j].view(hkv, group, HEAD_DIM), kb) * cfg["sm_scale"]
            out[b, j] = torch.einsum("kgt,tkd->kgd", att.softmax(-1), vb).reshape(hq, HEAD_DIM)
    out = _rms(out) * torch.sigmoid(gate.float()).view(batch, length, hq, HEAD_DIM)
    return out.reshape(batch, length, hq * HEAD_DIM), k_new, v_new


def collect(data, output) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Runs in the submission's process after a step: the output followed by the new cache
    entries, as raw bytes (see unpack)."""
    cfg = data["config"]
    shape = (cfg["batch"], cfg["q_len"], cfg["num_q_heads"] * HEAD_DIM)
    if type(output) is not torch.Tensor or output.dtype != torch.bfloat16 or tuple(output.shape) != shape:
        raise ValueError(f"expected a bfloat16 tensor of shape {shape}")
    slots = new_slots(data)
    hkv = cfg["num_kv_heads"]
    k = data["k_cache"].view(-1, hkv, HEAD_DIM)[slots]
    v = data["v_cache"].view(-1, hkv, HEAD_DIM)[slots]
    return torch.cat([p.contiguous().view(torch.uint8).reshape(-1) for p in (output, k, v)])


def unpack(raw: torch.Tensor, cfg: dict):
    b, length, hq, hkv = cfg["batch"], cfg["q_len"], cfg["num_q_heads"], cfg["num_kv_heads"]
    shapes = [((b, length, hq * HEAD_DIM), torch.bfloat16), ((b, length, hkv, HEAD_DIM), FP8),
              ((b, length, hkv, HEAD_DIM), FP8)]
    sizes = [math.prod(shape) * dtype.itemsize for shape, dtype in shapes]
    if raw.dtype != torch.uint8 or raw.numel() != sum(sizes):
        return None
    out, at = [], 0
    for (shape, dtype), n in zip(shapes, sizes):
        out.append(raw[at:at + n].view(dtype).view(shape))
        at += n
    return out


def check_implementation(data, raw):
    parts = unpack(raw, data["config"])
    if parts is None:
        return False, "malformed output"
    out, k, v = parts
    _, ref_k, ref_v = ref_kernel(data)
    for name, got, want, scale in (("key", k, ref_k, data["k_scale"]), ("value", v, ref_v, data["v_scale"])):
        ok, kv_msg = compare(_dequant(got, scale), _dequant(want, scale), CACHE_TOL)
        if not ok:
            return False, f"new {name} cache entries: {kv_msg}"
    # The output is checked against the reference attending the submission's own new cache
    # entries (checked above), since FP8 rounding of those entries varies by implementation.
    ref = ref_kernel(data, new_kv=(k, v))[0].to(torch.bfloat16)
    e4m3 = relative_l2(ref_kernel(data, torch.float8_e4m3fn, new_kv=(k, v))[0].to(torch.bfloat16), ref)
    tol = query_precision_bound(e4m3, FP8_QUERY_FACTOR, FP8_QUERY_FLOOR, REL_L2_TOL, FP8_QUERY_SLACK)
    ok, msg = compare(out, ref, tol)
    msg = (f"{msg} [bound {tol:.3f}: {FP8_QUERY_FACTOR:g} x the reference's {e4m3:.3f} with FP8 E4M3 queries"
           f" + {FP8_QUERY_SLACK:g}]")
    return ok, msg


def speed_of_light_ns(batch: int, ctx: int, heads: str, layer: str, hw: dict, q_len: int = 1,
                      spread: str = "fixed", **_) -> float:
    hq, hkv = HEADS[heads]
    attended = min(ctx, SLIDING_WINDOW) if layer == "sliding" else ctx
    # Uneven lengths average about ctx but can sit below it; stay a lower bound.
    tokens = batch * attended * _shortest_share(spread)
    bytes_moved = tokens * hkv * HEAD_DIM * 2 + batch * q_len * (2 * hq + 2 * hkv) * HEAD_DIM * 2 * 2
    flops = 4.0 * tokens * q_len * hq * HEAD_DIM
    return 1e9 * max(bytes_moved / hw["hbm_bytes_per_s"], flops / hw["bf16_dense_flops_per_s"])

"""Starter: the attention step in plain PyTorch, correct but slow. Each request attends over
every position its page table can hold in the paged FP8 cache, with positions past its
context or outside the window masked out.

Implement kernel_fn."""

from typing import TypedDict

import torch


class Config(TypedDict):
    batch: int            # B
    q_len: int            # L: 1 for decode, 8 for a speculative verify block (causal inside it)
    num_q_heads: int      # Hq: 16 per GPU under TP8
    num_kv_heads: int     # Hkv: 2; each serves Hq / Hkv query heads
    head_dim: int         # 64
    page_size: int        # 1 in the scored cases (as SGLang serves Muse on H200), 64 in some tests
    window: int           # 2048 on sliding-window layers (a token and the 2,047 before it); 0 = all
    rope_theta: float     # 500000 on sliding-window layers; 0 = no RoPE
    qk_scale_factor: float
    sm_scale: float       # 1/8
    kv_scale: float       # the cache scales' value: 1 in the scored cases (SGLang leaves them unset)


class Inputs(TypedDict):
    qkv: torch.Tensor          # bfloat16 [B, L, (2*Hq + 2*Hkv)*64], 2304 under tp8: per token q (Hq*64),
                               # then the block's keys before norm and RoPE (Hkv*64), values
                               # (Hkv*64) and the output gate's logits (Hq*64)
    positions: torch.Tensor    # int64 [B*L], each new token's position (seq_lens[b] + i)
    cache_loc: torch.Tensor    # int64 [B*L], each new token's flat cache row (page * page_size + offset)
    cache_seqlens: torch.Tensor  # int32 [B], seq_lens + L: what each request attends over
    cu_seqlens_q: torch.Tensor   # int32 [B+1], 0, L, 2L, ...: the block's query offsets
    scheduler_metadata: torch.Tensor | None  # int32, FA3's tile schedule (get_scheduler_metadata) on
                                             # full-attention decode steps, else None
    k_cache: torch.Tensor     # float8_e4m3fn [pages, page_size, Hkv, 64], written in place
    v_cache: torch.Tensor     # float8_e4m3fn [pages, page_size, Hkv, 64], written in place
    k_scale: torch.Tensor     # float32 [], key = e4m3 * k_scale
    v_scale: torch.Tensor     # float32 [], value = e4m3 * v_scale
    page_table: torch.Tensor  # int32 [B, max_pages], physical page of each logical page (-1 unused)
    seq_lens: torch.Tensor    # int32 [B], cached tokens per request; the block starts at this position
    config: Config


def rms(x, eps=1e-5):
    x = x.float()
    return x * torch.rsqrt(x.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True) + eps)


def rope(x, pos, theta):
    """Interleaved (GPT-J) RoPE: pairs (2i, 2i+1) rotate by pos * theta^(-2i/d)."""
    d = x.shape[-1]
    inv_freq = 1.0 / (theta ** (torch.arange(0, d, 2, device=x.device).float() / d))
    ang = pos.float()[..., None] * inv_freq
    cos, sin = ang.cos().unsqueeze(-2), ang.sin().unsqueeze(-2)
    even, odd = x[..., 0::2], x[..., 1::2]
    return torch.stack([even * cos - odd * sin, even * sin + odd * cos], -1).flatten(-2)


def kernel_fn(data: Inputs) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Normalize the queries and new keys (scaleless RMSNorm, queries also times
    qk_scale_factor), apply RoPE on sliding-window layers, write the block's keys and values
    into the FP8 cache at positions seq_lens[b] .. seq_lens[b] + L - 1, attend (each token sees
    the cache and the block's tokens up to itself), then return rmsnorm(attention) *
    sigmoid(gate) as bfloat16 [B, L, Hq*64]."""
    cfg = data["config"]
    batch, length = cfg["batch"], cfg["q_len"]
    hq, hkv, d, page = cfg["num_q_heads"], cfg["num_kv_heads"], cfg["head_dim"], cfg["page_size"]
    q_in, k_in, v_in, gate = data["qkv"].split([hq * d, hkv * d, hkv * d, hq * d], -1)
    pos = data["positions"].view(batch, length)  # [B, L]
    q = rms(q_in.reshape(batch, length, hq, d)) * cfg["qk_scale_factor"]
    k = rms(k_in.reshape(batch, length, hkv, d))
    if cfg["rope_theta"]:
        q, k = rope(q, pos, cfg["rope_theta"]), rope(k, pos, cfg["rope_theta"])
    q = q.to(torch.bfloat16)

    table = data["page_table"].long()
    slots = data["cache_loc"].view(batch, length)  # [B, L]
    k_cache = data["k_cache"].view(-1, hkv, d)
    v_cache = data["v_cache"].view(-1, hkv, d)
    k_scale, v_scale = data["k_scale"], data["v_scale"]
    k_cache[slots] = (k / k_scale).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    v_cache[slots] = (v_in.reshape(batch, length, hkv, d).float() / v_scale).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)

    # Every position a request's page table can hold; unused pages (-1) read page 0 and
    # are masked out with everything else past the token's own position.
    t = torch.arange(table.shape[1] * page, device=q.device)
    out = torch.empty((batch, length, hq, d), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=q.device)
    for b in range(batch):
        rows = table[b].clamp(min=0)[t // page] * page + t % page
        keys = k_cache[rows].float() * k_scale  # [S, Hkv, d]
        vals = v_cache[rows].float() * v_scale
        visible = t[None, :] <= pos[b][:, None]  # [L, S]: causal, including the block's own tokens
        if cfg["window"]:
            visible &= t[None, :] > pos[b][:, None] - cfg["window"]
        att = torch.einsum("lkgd,skd->lkgs", q[b].view(length, hkv, hq // hkv, d).float(), keys) * cfg["sm_scale"]
        att = att.masked_fill(~visible[:, None, None, :], float("-inf")).softmax(-1)
        out[b] = torch.einsum("lkgs,skd->lkgd", att, vals).reshape(length, hq, d)
    out = rms(out) * torch.sigmoid(gate.float()).view(batch, length, hq, d)
    return out.reshape(batch, length, hq * d).to(torch.bfloat16)

task_md:
# Gated attention decode (`muse_attention_decode`)

One decode step or 8-token verify block of grouped-query attention over a paged FP8 cache: QK-norm, a 2,048-token sliding window with RoPE or full attention over the whole context, and a gated, normalized output.

Your job is to compute this faster than SGLang's kernel does. Beside this file, `okc init` wrote:

- `submission.py`, your kernel. It starts as a plain PyTorch version of the computation. Keep its first line, `# okc: problem=muse_attention_decode`: it tells `okc submit` the problem.
- `baseline.py`, SGLang's kernel: the one you're timed against.
- `reference.py`, the computation as the judge checks it: `generate_input`, the reference and the correctness checks, with `checks.py` beside it: the spec your output must meet. The judge uses its own copies, and runs them with steps of its own (the weights, routing fields, fresh inputs), so to check a change, use `okc check`.
- `AGENTS.md`, notes for a coding agent, if you use one.

## What to compute

```python
# per request b and block token j, at position p = positions[t]
q, k, v, gate = split(qkv[t])   # the fused projection output
q = rmsnorm(q) * 5.473;  k = rmsnorm(k)
q, k = rope(q, p), rope(k, p)   # sliding layers
cache[cache_loc[t]] = fp8(k), fp8(v)
a = softmax(q @ K.T / 8) @ V    # up to p: window or all
out = rmsnorm(a) * sigmoid(gate)
```

`kernel_fn(data)` is the timed call and returns bfloat16 [B, L, Hq·64]. The `Inputs` and `Config` classes in submission.py give every field's dtype and shape; return GPU tensors of exactly that shape and dtype.

## Shapes

- B is batch and L is q_len: 1 for a decode step, or 8 for a speculative verify block (causal inside it). Each GPU has 16 query heads and 2 key/value heads (TP8).
- Each load times a sliding-window layer (the last 2,048 tokens, with RoPE) and a full-attention layer (the whole context, no RoPE). Contexts are around 80K tokens.
- The inputs are what SGLang’s attention receives: the fused projection output, plus the step’s positions, cache rows and FA3 lengths, which SGLang builds once per step.
- `scheduler_metadata` is FA3's tile schedule for the step, built from its lengths as SGLang does: set on full-attention decode steps, None on sliding layers and verify blocks. Kernels that don't use FA3 can ignore it.
- The cache is FP8 E4M3. Its page size is 1 in the scored cases and 64 in most tests, so read config["page_size"]. Its scales are 1 in the scored cases and 1/64 in some tests.
- Decode loads are SGLang serving with speculative decoding off; verify loads are its default recipe, which checks each request's 8-token draft in one step.

| load | shape | weight | floor |
|---|---|---|---|
| decode 1 | batch 1, ctx 80000, heads tp8, layer sliding, page 1, dist soft | 46 | 0.1 µs |
| decode 1 | batch 1, ctx 80000, heads tp8, layer full, page 1, dist coherent | 16 | 4.3 µs |
| decode 16 | batch 16, ctx 80000, heads tp8, layer sliding, page 1, spread agentic, dist soft | 46 | 1.6 µs |
| decode 16 | batch 16, ctx 80000, heads tp8, layer full, page 1, spread agentic, dist coherent | 16 | 63.2 µs |
| decode 32 | batch 32, ctx 80000, heads tp8, layer sliding, page 1, spread agentic, dist soft | 46 | 3.3 µs |
| decode 32 | batch 32, ctx 80000, heads tp8, layer full, page 1, spread agentic, dist coherent | 16 | 126.4 µs |
| verify 1 | batch 1, ctx 80000, heads tp8, layer sliding, page 1, q_len 8, dist soft | 46 | 0.1 µs |
| verify 1 | batch 1, ctx 80000, heads tp8, layer full, page 1, q_len 8, dist coherent | 16 | 4.3 µs |
| verify 16 | batch 16, ctx 80000, heads tp8, layer sliding, page 1, q_len 8, spread agentic, dist soft | 46 | 1.9 µs |
| verify 16 | batch 16, ctx 80000, heads tp8, layer full, page 1, q_len 8, spread agentic, dist coherent | 16 | 63.4 µs |
| verify 32 | batch 32, ctx 80000, heads tp8, layer sliding, page 1, q_len 8, spread agentic, dist soft | 46 | 3.7 µs |
| verify 32 | batch 32, ctx 80000, heads tp8, layer full, page 1, q_len 8, spread agentic, dist coherent | 16 | 126.8 µs |

A shape's weight is how many times one step runs it. A load's time is the sum of its shapes' times, each times its weight. Your speedup on the problem is the geometric mean, over loads, of SGLang's load time over yours, so each load counts equally. The time shown for a run is SGLang's time per step, averaged over loads the same way, divided by that speedup.

The floor is the time to move the data at 4.8 TB/s or do the math at 989 TFLOP/s, whichever is longer.

## Correctness

Every test and every timed call is checked against a reference. Errors are relative L2, |out − ref| / |ref|:

- The output: within 2.5× the reference's own error when its queries are rounded to FP8 E4M3, plus 1.5%, kept between 3% and 15%, against an FP32 reference.
- The new cache entries: within 8% of the reference's. Your output is checked against the reference attending to your own new entries.
- Some tests put keys at the window's edges.
- Each head's keys share a direction, so attention spreads over many keys. On full layers the low-attention keys' values share a direction too.
- Any single row: at most 5× its bound. A near-zero row is measured against a tenth of the average row.
- No NaN or Inf.

## How a run is timed

- Each shape is captured as a CUDA graph and timed by replaying it, in the same run and on the same GPU as SGLang's kernel, your replays and SGLang's taking turns on the same fresh inputs.
- Every timed replay starts with a cold L2: the judge reads a buffer larger than L2 just before it.
- A shape's speedup is the median of paired ratios: each repetition's SGLang time over yours, taken two repetitions at a time with the order swapped, so which side went first cancels. Your time on the shape is SGLang's median time over that speedup.
- Each run reports its speedup with a 95% interval (at least ±1.5%). Gains inside the interval might be noise.
- The judge subtracts a graph replay's fixed cost (about 4 µs) from both sides.

## Rules

- **CUDA graphs.** The timed calls replay `kernel_fn` as a CUDA graph: no host syncs (`.item()`, `.cpu()`, `torch.cuda.synchronize()`, printing a tensor), and no allocating or branching on input values. Branching on shapes and `config` is fine.
- **Fresh inputs.** Every call gets new inputs; don't cache anything derived from `data`.
- **Activations.** BF16 wherever SGLang's kernel keeps BF16. The KV cache stays FP8; queries may be rounded to FP8 E4M3, as FA3 does, and no coarser.
- **Every key.** Attend to the whole 2,048-token window on sliding layers and the whole context on full ones: no top-k, sparse or block-skipping attention, and no skipping values by their attention weight.
- **Checked before running.** A submission is rejected if it patches timing, reads harness frames, touches harness I/O or secrets, edits loaded modules, imports the reference, starts processes or uses the network.

Full rules: https://openkernelchallenge.dev/rules

## Submitting

```bash
okc submit submission.py      # the tests, then timing; waits for the result
okc check submission.py       # the same run, kept off the board
okc status <job>              # a run's result again
okc jobs                      # your recent runs
```

A failing run names its first failing case and why. A passing run shows each shape's time against SGLang's and your speedup, and okc saves a profile beside your file, in `profiles/submission.<job>.txt`, showing where the time goes.

`print()` is fine for diagnostics (just not a tensor's values inside `kernel_fn`, which syncs). The last 16,000 characters of what a run prints come back with it, passing or not: okc saves it to `profiles/submission.<job>.log`, and `okc status <job> --json` has it as `log_tail`.

Runs on this problem have a daily limit, and the same code again returns its earlier result. `okc withdraw <job>` takes a run off the board. A check run (`okc check`) is the same run kept off the board and out of your attempts, for experiments, with a daily limit of its own. `okc problems` shows today's limits and what you have left; they reset at 00:00 UTC.

A run has 15 minutes in all, compiling included; one that runs past that is charged as a timeout.

## Where you stand

```bash
okc leaderboard muse_attention_decode
```

Your best run is your row on the board, which is on the site too, at https://openkernelchallenge.dev/problems/muse_attention_decode. It also counts toward the overall kernel board (`okc leaderboard`), which ranks by how much your best runs together would speed up a decode step.
